mainTopic: Does a person ever pay a debt before it is due? Proofs for ריש לקיש and אביי ורבא from the wall משנה, the final הלכה, and whether מה לי לשקר can override the חזקה.
overview: Just before this point, ריש לקיש held that a borrower is not believed when he says he paid before the due date, because people do not pay early. אביי ורבא held that people sometimes do pay early, to stop the lender from bothering them. The גמרא tries to prove אביי ורבא right from the משנה about two neighbors building a wall. That proof is pushed away, because each finished row of the wall is its own due date. Then the גמרא tries to prove ריש לקיש right from a later line of the same משנה. That proof is also pushed away, because that neighbor doubted he would owe anything at all. After reporting that different אמוראים ruled each way, the גמרא decides the הלכה follows ריש לקיש, even when collecting from orphans without an oath. Finally, a new question opens: if the lender demands payment after the due date, can the borrower's מה לי לשקר beat the חזקה? That discussion continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Why someone might pay early: to avoid being bothered
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of the reasoning of אביי ורבא: a person may pay early so the lender will not keep pestering him.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that he will not keep bothering me.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes the explanation of אביי ורבא for why a person sometimes pays a debt before it is due. He pays early so the lender will not keep coming after him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש assumed nobody pays early. אביי ורבא answer that a person who happens to have money on hand may pay early, simply to get rid of the lender's nagging. This sets up the whole question the rest of the section tries to prove.

keyTerms.meaning: So that / in order that
He will bother me / trouble me

phrases.english: so that he will not bother me.
phrases.notes: This is the borrower talking. If he pays now, the lender will stop chasing him for the money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reasoning of אביי ורבא from just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person sometimes pays a debt early so the lender will not keep pestering him.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: he is presumed to have paid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: a neighbor is assumed to have paid his share of the wall unless there is proof he did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: He is presumed to have paid, unless the other one brings proof that he did not pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה about the wall. This sets up an attempt to prove that אביי ורבא are right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, one neighbor claims the other never paid his share of the wall. The משנה says we assume he did pay, unless there is proof he did not. The next step will ask what exact case this is, to see if it shows that people pay early.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned (in a משנה)
Presumed to be / assumed to be
Proof

phrases.english: We learned: He is presumed to have given,
phrases.notes: This is the wall משנה from the previous עמוד, about the neighbor's share of the cost.

phrases.english: unless he brings proof that he did not give.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to test the view of אביי ורבא just stated.
steps.raayaObject: The view of אביי ורבא that people sometimes pay early.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: the neighbor is presumed to have paid his share of the wall.

steps.title: The case must be early payment, so people do pay early
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that the משנה cannot mean payment on time, because that is obvious. It must mean payment before the due date, which proves that people pay early.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If he told him, 'I paid you on time,' then it is obvious that we assume he paid! Rather, isn't it that he told him, 'I paid you before the due date'? So we see that a person does pay before his due date!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what case the משנה is talking about. It concludes that the case must be someone who claims he paid early, so this proves אביי ורבא are right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he claimed he paid on time, there would be nothing new for the משנה to teach. So the משנה must mean he claims he paid while the wall was still being built, before the money was due. Since we believe him, it shows people really do pay early, like אביי ורבא, and unlike ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? / How do we picture it?
It is obvious
Within my time, meaning before the due date
So we see / apparently

steps.confusionAlert: 'בתוך זמני' does NOT mean 'on time.' It means 'within the period before the deadline,' meaning early. 'בזמני' is the one that means on time.

phrases.english: What is the case?
If you say he told him: 'I paid you at my due time,'
phrases.notes: On time here means once the wall was finished and the money was due.

phrases.english: it is obvious that he is presumed to have given!
Rather, isn't it that he told him:
'I paid you before my due time'?
So we see that a person does
pay it before its due time!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the quoted משנה to pull out the proof.
steps.raayaObject: אביי ורבא: people sometimes pay before the due date.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's ruling must be about a claim of early payment, because a claim of on-time payment would be too obvious to teach.

steps.title: Rejected: with a wall, every row has its own due date
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. With a wall, the money is due after each row is finished, so paying during construction is not really paying early.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different here, because each and every row is its own due date.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof for אביי ורבא. Paying while the wall is being built is actually paying on time, row by row.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed the due date was the end of the whole wall. The גמרא answers that each finished row of the wall creates its own payment due. So the משנה can be talking about on-time payment, and the משנה tells us nothing about whether people pay early.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different here
A row / layer of stones in a wall
Its due time

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה about the wall does not prove that people pay early, because each row of the wall is its own due date.

phrases.english: It is different here,
because each and every row is its due time.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only this proof. It does not disprove the view of אביי ורבא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof wrongly assumed one due date at the end of the wall. Really, each row is its own due date.

steps.title: A new attempt: he is presumed not to have paid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the next line of the משנה, where the neighbor is presumed NOT to have paid. This sets up a possible proof for ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: He is presumed not to have paid, unless he brings proof that he did pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new attempted proof, this time to support ריש לקיש, from a later case in the same משנה. This step is only the setup; the analysis comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this later case, the neighbor who did not want a tall wall later built a wall of his own next to it so he could put a roof on it. Now he must pay for the full height. Here the משנה says the opposite: we assume he did NOT pay unless he proves it. The גמרא will next ask what this case is, to see if it shows that people do not pay early.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introduces a proof)
That he did not give / did not pay

phrases.english: Come and hear: He is presumed not to have given,
phrases.notes: This is the later case in the wall משנה, where he built a second wall to put a roof over the space.

phrases.english: unless he brings proof that he gave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof for אביי ורבא was rejected, the גמרא opens a new proof from the same משנה, apparently for ריש לקיש.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש: a person does not pay before the due date.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The later case in the wall משנה: the neighbor is presumed not to have paid.

steps.title: Proving ריש לקיש from the second line of the wall משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what claim the neighbor is making in the משנה's case where he is not believed. If he says 'I paid on time,' there is no reason to doubt him. So he must be saying 'I paid early,' which shows people do not pay early.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If the neighbor said, 'I paid you when it was due,' why would he not be believed? It must be that he said, 'I paid you before it was due.' So we see that people do not usually pay before the due date!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof it set up in Step 5. It argues that the משנה's line about not believing the neighbor only makes sense if he claimed he paid early.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A claim of paying on time would normally be believed, so that cannot be why the משנה rejects him. The only claim left is 'I paid early.' If the משנה does not believe that claim, it shows the חזקה that people do not pay early, just as ריש לקיש says.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What exactly are the circumstances?
If you say (offering a first possibility)
Rather, is it not that... (pushing to the only remaining option)
Apparently / so we see
Within his time, meaning before the payment is due

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If we say that he said to him:
"I paid you at my due time,"
why would he not be believed?
Rather, is it not that he said to him:
"I paid you within my time" (before it was due)?
Apparently a person does not usually
pay before his due time!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof that Step 5 set up by quoting the משנה's second line.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's view that a borrower is not believed when he says he paid before the due date.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's case where the neighbor is presumed not to have paid; the only claim that would not be believed is 'I paid early.'

steps.title: This neighbor would never pay early because he doubted he owed anything
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. In this case the neighbor was not sure the court would make him pay at all, so of course he would not pay early. That tells us nothing about ordinary loans.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it is different. The neighbor thinks: 'Who says the רבנן will make me pay at all?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof for ריש לקיש. It explains that this neighbor had a special reason not to pay early.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The neighbor was not sure he would ever have to pay for the wall, so he would wait to see if the court would obligate him. Not believing him here says nothing about a normal borrower, who knows he owes the money. So the proof for ריש לקיש falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it is different (this case is special)
Who says? (expressing doubt)
They will obligate (make someone pay)

phrases.english: Here it is different,
because he says (to himself):
Who says that the רבנן will obligate me to pay?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from Step 6 by showing the case is special.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof only; it does not prove ריש לקיש wrong.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The neighbor's doubt about owing anything gives him his own reason not to pay early, so the case cannot teach a general rule about borrowers.

steps.title: How the אמוראים actually ruled
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע ruled like אביי ורבא. מר בר רב אשי ruled like ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע acted like אביי ורבא. מר בר רב אשי acted like ריש לקיש.
steps.whatsHappening: The proofs are over, and now the גמרא reports what judges actually did in real cases. This sets up the final ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proofs back and forth did not settle the debate, so the גמרא looks at practice. Some judges believed a borrower who said he paid early, like אביי ורבא. Others did not, like ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: They acted like... (ruled in practice like this opinion)
An אמורא, the son of רב אשי

phrases.aramaic: רַב פָּפָּא וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
phrases.english: Rav Pappa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua
acted in accordance with Abaye and Rava.

phrases.aramaic: מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי עָבֵד כְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ.
phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi acted in accordance with Reish Lakish.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא וְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ עָבְדִי כְּאַבַּיֵּי וְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proofs fail, the גמרא turns to how the dispute was ruled in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Some אמוראים ruled like אביי ורבא and others like ריש לקיש.

steps.title: The הלכה follows ריש לקיש, even against orphans
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה is like ריש לקיש. A borrower is not believed when he says he paid early. The lender can even collect from the borrower's orphans without the usual oath, because of the חזקה that people do not pay early.
steps.simpleTranslation: The הלכה is like ריש לקיש, even when collecting from orphans. Normally someone collecting from orphans' property must swear first. Here he does not, because there is a חזקה that people do not pay before the due date.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling: a borrower who says he paid early is not believed. It adds that this holds even when the lender collects from the borrower's orphans.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, someone collecting a debt from orphans must swear he was not already paid. We do this because the orphans cannot know what their father paid. Here no oath is needed, because the חזקה is so strong that we assume no early payment ever happened.

keyTerms.meaning: And the הלכה is (the final practical ruling)
Orphans
An oath
A presumption based on how people normally act
The Master said (quoting an earlier teaching)

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows ריש לקיש. Because of the חזקה that people do not pay early, a borrower who claims he paid before the due date is not believed. The lender collects even from orphans, with no oath.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical bottom line of the whole debate. It also shows how strong this חזקה is, since it even removes the oath we usually require to protect orphans.

phrases.english: And the halacha is in accordance with Reish Lakish,
and even from orphans;
phrases.notes: If the borrower died, the lender can still collect from the heirs based on this rule.

phrases.english: and even though the Master said:
one who comes to collect from the property of orphans
may collect only with an oath;
still, there is a presumption: a person does not usually
pay before his due time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the split in practice reported in Step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה is like ריש לקיש: a claim of early payment is not believed, and the lender collects even from orphans without an oath, because of the חזקה.

steps.title: Does 'why would I lie' beat the חזקה?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: the lender demands payment after the due date, and the borrower says he paid early. He could have said 'I paid on time' and been believed. Does that better possible lie make him believable, even against the חזקה?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: The lender asked for his money after the due date, and the borrower said, 'I paid you before it was due.' What is the law? Do we say that even against a חזקה, we apply 'why would I lie?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. It is setting up a discussion about whether the rule of מה לי לשקר can override the חזקה that people do not pay early.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the due date has passed, the borrower could simply have said 'I paid on time' and been believed. Since he chose a weaker claim, maybe he is telling the truth (מה לי לשקר). The question is whether that reasoning works even against a חזקה; the other side of the question comes on the next עמוד.

keyTerms.meaning: It was asked of them (an open question among the חכמים)
He demanded payment from him
After the due date
Why would I lie? (he could have made a better claim, so we believe him)
Where there is a presumption against him

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the earlier case. Before, the lender asked for payment right when the due date arrived. Now he asks after the due date has already passed, so the borrower had an easy lie available: 'I paid on time.'

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
If he demanded payment after the due date,
and the borrower said to him: "I paid you within my time,"
what is the law?
Do we say: even where there is a presumption
we still say "why would I lie?";
phrases.notes: He could have lied better by saying 'I paid on time,' which would have been believed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the ruling for ריש לקיש by asking whether the חזקה still wins when the borrower has a מה לי לשקר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether מה לי לשקר can make a borrower believable even against the חזקה that people do not pay early.
